access_method: Official REST API with an API key (src/collect_youtube.py); search.list then videos.list then commentThreads.list; regionCode=IN
fields_collected: video id, title, channel id, published_at, view/like/comment counts; top-level comment id, text, like count, published_at
granularity: daily snapshot per product (counts are cumulative at collection time)
limitations: Default quota 10,000 units/day plus 100 search.list calls/day (each list call costs 1 unit); search results are a relevance-ranked sample, not all videos; like counts can be hidden; comments can be disabled; history is not available, so trends need repeated snapshots
terms_note: Subject to the YouTube API Services Terms of Service and Developer Policies (data storage and refresh rules apply); API key kept in .env and never committed

access_method: Manual CSV export from trends.google.com (Interest over time), saved untouched to raw/trends/ and parsed by src/load_trends.py
fields_collected: relative search interest (0-100) per date for one search term; India; Web Search; All categories
granularity: weekly for a 12-month window (daily for windows of 90 days or less)
limitations: Values are relative and rescaled per export (peak=100), so they are not absolute volumes; '<1' values stored as 0.5; low-volume terms return zeros; manual process, so settings must be kept identical
terms_note: Used under the Google Terms of Service via the public website; no scraping or unofficial APIs; cite Google Trends as the source

access_method: Manual CSV export from trends.google.com (Interest over time) with a custom time range, saved untouched to raw/trends/ and parsed by src/load_trends.py
fields_collected: relative search interest (0-100) per day for one search term; India; Web Search; All categories
granularity: daily; window changed on 2026-10-03 from 12 months weekly to a 269-day custom range (about 9 months), identical for every product; supersedes the earlier Google Trends row
limitations: Daily data is only returned for ranges of 269 days or less (secondary sources, not official docs); values rescaled per export (peak=100); '<1' stored as 0.5; loader rejects weekly or monthly files and mismatched date ranges
terms_note: Used under the Google Terms of Service via the public website; no scraping or unofficial APIs; cite Google Trends as the source

access_method: Official REST API with an API key (src/collect_youtube.py). Main pass: search.list (order=relevance, maxResults=50) then videos.list then commentThreads.list for the top 5 videos by views. Recent pass (added 2026-10-03): one search.list with order=date and publishedAfter=run time - 7 days. regionCode=IN. Queries come from the active registry version (v3 since 2026-10-03), and every row and raw file carries its query_version.
fields_collected: as before, plus: videos_published_7d, videos_7d_on_target and cap_hit (recent pass); search_total_results_approx and result_cap_hit (main pass). Cleaned daily table adds title-based exact-model (on-target) totals.
granularity: one snapshot per product per run day; recent pass counts uploads in a rolling 7-day window
limitations: As in the earlier YouTube row. In addition: video_result_count is capped at 50 and carries no signal; recent-pass counts are capped at 50 and include loose matches (6-83% exact-model in the pilot); order=date depends on the search index and can miss new uploads; on-target filtering is a title heuristic; the -term exclusion operator did not reliably remove sibling-model videos (registry v2 test).
terms_note: Subject to the YouTube API Services Terms of Service and Developer Policies; API key kept in .env and never committed; raw responses and comment tables kept out of the public repo.

access_method: Automated, via the pytrends library (src/collect_trends_pytrends.py). It calls Google's unofficial web endpoints with the same settings as the manual export: geo IN, cat 0, Web Search, timeframe 2026-01-08 2026-10-03, one term per request. Native result saved to raw/trends/pytrends_native/; a website-layout copy goes to raw/trends/ for the loader.
fields_collected: relative search interest (0-100) per day for one term, plus isPartial
limitations: Integers only: '<1' comes back as 0, so is_below_threshold cannot be set and zeros mix true zeros with '<1'. Last day can be partial (isPartial). Values are rescaled per request (peak = 100), as with the website export.
terms_note: Not an official API: pytrends uses Google's unofficial web endpoints and may break or be blocked at any time. Rate-limited politely (30-75 s pauses, 60/120/240 s backoff, stop after 3 consecutive failures); no proxies, spoofing or identity rotation.
